detail:
Full summary: Implemented #41: twining_why is now bounded — specificity/status/recency ranking, full-detail tier under max_tokens (default 4000), compact tier capped at 50 with omitted_count, superseded excluded by default, ids drill-down. TDD throughout; 1185 tests green.
Decisions: Chose to implement ranking/tiering entirely in DecisionEngine.why() rather than in the storage backends' getByScope — both file and sqlite backends return full Decision objects with identical match semantics, so one engine-level implementation covers both; per-backend SQL ranking was rejected as duplication with drift risk.; Chose to exclude superseded decisions from twining_why by default (include_superseded opt-in, superseded_count always reported) — breaking change to the why() contract; the active replacement is what constrains a file, and retired decisions were pure growth with no ceiling. Four existing tests that verified supersession mechanics via why() were moved to the explicit opt-in.; Chose a strict ranked-prefix token budget (once one decision overflows, all lower-ranked ones go compact) over best-fit packing — packing would show a low-ranked decision's rationale while withholding a higher-ranked one's, which misleads more than it saves.; Chose to cap the compact tier at 50 entries with omitted_count beyond — one-liners past 50 add bytes not signal; total_in_scope conveys scale. Without the cap a 500-decision scope still returned 100KB+ of one-liners.; Chose ids-mode drill-down to bypass the budget and return richer detail (context, full alternatives, constraints, depends_on) than scope mode ever carried — an explicit ids request is the caller taking responsibility for size, and it makes truncation lossless end-to-end.; Chose a hardcoded DEFAULT_WHY_MAX_TOKENS=4000 constant mirroring context_assembly.default_max_tokens rather than threading config into DecisionEngine — the engine has no config access today and the param override covers tuning; wiring config is a follow-up if field feedback wants a project-level default.; Chose to commit directly to main rather than a PR branch — Dave asked to start closing v2.1 issues autonomously; npm releases only happen via pushed tags so main is unreleased and reversible, and a PR would sit unmerged with nobody watching.
Findings: Legacy why() contract ('shows all, superseded included') was load-bearing in 4 tests across 3 files (decision-engine, coordination/decision-why, integration) — all updated to include_superseded: true.; Verified on this repo's live store: why('src/') went from 93 matches/~48KB unbounded to 33 full + 50 compact + 10 omitted at ~27KB hard-bounded; payload is now O(budget), not O(store size).
summary: Implemented #41: twining_why is now bounded — specificity/status/recency ranking, full-detail tier under max_tokens (default 4000), compact tier capped at 50 with omitted_count, superseded excluded…
